Stack: Once UI (`@once-ui-system/core` 3.0 beta) is installed and its standard providers are mounted in the root layout; its agent documentation is in the `docs/` folder, which you can read (start with `docs/AGENTS.md`).

Task: The signed-in shell of Lumen. Three screens share one layout: a dashboard at `/` (a welcome line and a few summary cards), a projects list at `/projects`, and a settings page at `/settings`. The navigation has nested groups: an "Analytics" group containing "Overview" and "Reports", and a "Workspace" group containing "Projects" and "Settings". The current route is highlighted in the navigation. A header shows a breadcrumb for the current screen. On phones the sidebar is replaced by a menu button that opens the navigation in a drawer.

- Brand colour #0F766E: primary buttons, the current navigation item, links and focus rings.
- Neutrals: cool slate grey.
- Corner radius: 2px on buttons, inputs, cards and menus.
- Headings in Georgia, "Times New Roman", serif; body text in ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif.
- Default theme: light.
- Density: compact: tight rows and small controls, information-dense.

# @once-ui-system/core — agent harness

This package ships an agent-first codegen harness under `ai/`, next to this file. Use it when **writing Once UI code**, not full MDX documentation pages. Paths below are relative to this file (in an app: `node_modules/@once-ui-system/core/`).

## Starting an app

A new signed-in app (sidebar, top bar, content panel) starts from `ai/starters/app/`: a working Next.js App Router setup with Once UI's CSS, fonts, providers and theme in `src/app/layout.tsx`, the shell mounted once in `src/app/(app)/layout.tsx`, and two pages. Copy it over the create-next-app files, then edit it rather than rewriting it:

```bash
cp -r node_modules/@once-ui-system/core/ai/starters/app/src/. src/ && rm -f src/app/page.module.css src/app/globals.css
```

No `src/` folder? Copy into the project root instead.

Can't run shell commands (you can only read files and reply with code)? Then nothing was copied, and an import of `AppShell` or `resources/app` breaks the build. Write the starter files your code imports (`components/AppShell.tsx`, `resources/app.ts`) in your reply, taking their content from `ai/starters/app/src/`, keep the project's own `app/layout.tsx`, and import only files you write or have opened in the project.

The copy takes `src/` only: also set `experimental.optimizePackageImports: ["@once-ui-system/core"]` in `next.config`, as `ai/starters/app/next.config.ts` does, or every route that imports the package root from a server component ships about 110 kB of extra JavaScript. That setting only works with webpack. Under Turbopack (the default for `next build` in Next 16), a server component should import client components from their own path, `@once-ui-system/core/components/Button`, so that it does not ship every component.

- `src/resources/app.ts`: product name, user and nav. The sidebar, breadcrumb and ⌘K palette all read it. Each nav href needs a page under `src/app/(app)/`; copy `home/page.tsx`.
- `src/resources/once-ui.config.ts`: brand, accent, neutral and `defaultTheme` (`theme` itself stays `"system"`, or the theme switch stops working).
- `src/components/AppShell.tsx`: the frame. Change it only to change the frame; it already covers the app-shell bundle's quality bar.

Then build each page from the bundle below that fits it.

## Writing a page or feature

Every file you read is sent again on every later turn, so read what you need in one step, then write.

1. Pick the bundle below closest to what you are building and read it, together with any project files you need (in a Next.js app at least `app/layout.tsx`, which mounts the providers), in a single step. Open those project files by path: listing their folder first costs a turn, and every turn re-sends the bundle. A bundle is complete: the rules, every component's props, types, gotchas, the quality bar and a gold example. Read one bundle, not two: a second one doubles what every later turn re-sends, and a component it adds is cheaper as its `ai/components/<Name>.json` slice. Then write the code.
2. Need a component the bundle does not list? Every bundle has the components in the `page.md` row; the Adds column names what each one carries on top. Read the `ai/components/<Name>.json` of anything else your page needs in that same step, not after the bundle.
3. Nothing fits? Read `ai/bundles/page.md` (the rules and the common components) with the `ai/components/<Name>.json` slices your page needs, in one step. `ai/catalog.json` names every component with its purpose.

Never open `ai/spec.json`: it is the full machine spec, for tooling.

# Once UI — code generation rules

Rules for writing Once UI code. Follow every rule; each shows the correct form first.

## Before you build

When the request doesn't specify design intent, ask these five questions first (one short message, all at once), then build:

1. **Content style** — bold / restrained / conservative?
2. **Layout** — wide or narrow, centered or left-aligned?
3. **Color** — single accent, bold colors, visually distinct sections?
4. **Decoration** — gradients, MatrixFx, animated blobs, none?
5. **Imagery** — placeholder images, or avatars/logos/icons only?

If you can't ask (or the user says "you decide"), default to: restrained, centered with `maxWidth="m"` content, single brand accent, one subtle gradient (recipes.md #1), no placeholder images (use `Avatar`, `Logo`, `Icon`).

## Layout primitives

1. Use `Row` and `Column` for layout. `Flex` with `direction` is only for dynamic direction. A `Flex` with no direction at all is a `Row` (`Flex` defaults to row).

```tsx
// Good
<Column gap="16">...</Column>
// Bad
<Flex direction="column" gap="16">...</Flex>
```

2. Use shorthands — they replace multi-prop combinations:

| Write | Instead of |
|-------|------------|
| `fill` | `fillWidth fillHeight` |
| `fit` | `fitWidth fitHeight` |
| `center` | `horizontal="center" vertical="center"` |

```tsx
// Good
<Row fill center>...</Row>
// Bad
<Row fillWidth fillHeight horizontal="center" vertical="center">...</Row>
```

3. Never write a prop that equals its default, or one that another prop on the same element already implies. The spec marks defaults with `= value`. Common offenders:
   - `position="relative"` (default on all layout components)
   - `direction="row"` on `Row`, `direction="column"` on `Column`
   - `variant="primary"`, `size="m"` on `Button`
   - `fillWidth` beside `maxWidth` — `maxWidth` already fills the width up to the cap
   - `minWidth={0}` beside `fillWidth` — `fillWidth` already sets `min-width: 0`
   - a colour on `border` (or `borderTop`, `borderBottom`, `borderX`, …) that only restates the default — bare `border` draws the default border, `--default-border` (`neutral-alpha-weak` unless the app sets it in its custom CSS); name a colour only to deviate from it

```tsx
// Good
<Column maxWidth="l" border radius="l">
// Bad
<Column fillWidth maxWidth="l" minWidth={0} position="relative" border="neutral-alpha-weak" radius="l">
```

3b. `zIndex` belongs to a stacking group, not to a page. Use it only inside an isolated group that needs an order — a decorative absolute layer and the content sibling above it (rule 21), a sticky header over the pane it covers — and keep the values small within that group. A `zIndex` on a lone element, or a page-wide ladder of `zIndex={3}`, `{5}`, `{9}`, means the hierarchy is being managed by hand; restructure the tree instead.

## Spacing and sizing

4. Use spacing tokens, never raw CSS: `gap`, `padding`, `margin`, `paddingX/Y`, `marginX/Y` accept the full `SpacingToken` scale (`"0" "1" "2" "4" "8" "12" "16" "20" "24" "32" "40" "48" "56" "64" "80" "104" "128" "160"`, or `"xs" "s" "m" "l" "xl"`). The top of the scale is what rule 17 calls for between sections — it is not an extension, it is part of the same list.

```tsx
// Good
<Column gap="8" padding="24">
// Bad
<div style={{ gap: 8, padding: 24 }}>
```

5. `width`/`height`/`maxWidth`/`minHeight` (and every spacing and offset prop) accept a number on the **token scale** (`width={320}`: `n` renders as the token `"n"` would, n/16 rem scaled by `data-scaling`, so 320 px at the defaults), a spacing token string (`"16"`), or a CSS length string (`"40rem"`, `"50%"`, `"100dvh"`, `calc(…)`). Prefer tokens; write `"320px"` for a length that must not scale. `maxWidth={40}` is 2.5rem, not 40rem (2.x).

6. Only use `style={{}}` for things no token prop covers (e.g. `isolation`, custom filters). If a prop exists, the prop wins.

## Color and surfaces

7. Colors are semantic tokens, never hex/rgb: `{tone}-{weight}` or `{tone}-alpha-{weight}` where tone = `neutral | brand | accent | info | danger | warning | success` and weight = `weak | medium | strong`. A component's palette is its `tone` prop (Button, IconButton, Tag, Feedback, Toast, `addToast`, `StatusIndicator pulse`, gauges, Timeline items); `scheme` is a palette hue (`blue`, `green`…) on the plain StatusIndicator dot and Avatar's `statusIndicator`.
   - `background` also accepts `surface | overlay | page | transparent`
   - `onBackground` colors text/icons on a background
   - Inline SVG paint too: `fill="currentColor"` (colour the wrapper with `onBackground`) or a token, `stroke="var(--brand-solid-strong)"` — never `fill="#15D9EF"`

8. Standard surface recipe: `background="surface"` (or `"overlay"` over imagery) + `border` + `radius="l"`. Bare `border` is the default border; name a colour (`border="neutral-alpha-medium"`, `border="brand-alpha-medium"`) only when the surface should differ from it.

```tsx
<Column background="surface" border radius="l" padding="24" gap="16">
```

## Text

9. Use `Text` and `Heading` with `textVariant="{type}-{weight}-{size}"` (the same prop as on Flex; `variant` was 2.x): type = `body | heading | display | label | code`, weight = `default | strong`, size = `xs | s | m | l | xl`. Examples: `body-default-m`, `heading-strong-s`, `label-default-s`, `display-strong-m`.

10. If a layout component only wraps text, put `textVariant` (and `onBackground`) directly on it instead of nesting a `Text`:

```tsx
// Good
<Row textVariant="label-default-s" onBackground="neutral-weak">Updated today</Row>
// Bad
<Row><Text textVariant="label-default-s" onBackground="neutral-weak">Updated today</Text></Row>
```

## Responsive

11. Use breakpoint props (`xl l m s xs`) with override objects — never media queries or conditional rendering for layout:

```tsx
<Row gap="24" s={{ direction: "column" }}>
<Grid columns="3" s={{ columns: 1 }}>
```

Breakpoints, padding, background, border, radius, sizes and `hide` exist only on `Flex`, `Row`, `Column` and `Grid`. Leaf components (`Button`, the fields and controls, `Text`, `Heading`, `Icon`, `Avatar`, `Kbd`…) take `LeafProps` — margins, `flex`, `fillWidth`, `position` and offsets, `className`, `style` — so wrap one to change the rest: `<Row s={{ hide: true }}><Button …/></Row>`, `<Column padding="8"><Text …/></Column>`.

## Components over primitives

12. Reach for the purpose-built component before composing primitives:
    - `Card` is for **interactive** surfaces only (`href` or `onClick`). Static panels (pricing tiers, testimonials, stat boxes) = `Column`/`Row` with the surface recipe (#8), not `Card`
    - Image/video → `Media`, not `img`
    - Links → `SmartLink` / `Button href`, not `a`
    - Status dot → `StatusIndicator`; progress → `ProgressBar`; loading → `Spinner` / `Skeleton`
    - Labels/metadata → `Tag` (`variant="announce"` + `href` for the "New" pill above a hero; `selected` (+ `onClick`) or `onRemove` for a filter toggle), `Kbd`, `InlineCode`. Badge and Chip are Tag in 3.0
    - Tabs → `Tabs` > `TabList` > `Tab` with a `TabPanel` per value (`orientation="vertical"` for a settings nav). `SegmentedControl` picks a value; it is not a tab set
    - Mobile nav, filters, a side sheet → `Drawer` (`side`, `size`); it brings the focus trap, scroll lock and Escape a hand-made overlay misses
    - Where-am-I trail → `Breadcrumbs items={[{ label, href }, ...]}`; the last item is the current page
    - Keyboard shortcuts → `useHotkeys("mod+k", fn)` (it skips while the user types), shown with `Kbd keys="mod+k" label="Search"`
    - Text for screen readers only, skip links → `VisuallyHidden` (`focusable` for a skip link)
    - Markdown/MDX content → `mdxComponents` or `createMdxComponents({...})` from `/mdx` (rule 30), never a hand-written element map

13. Use the distinctive features when the design calls for them — they exist and are cheap:
    - `Dialog` supports `stack` (stacked dialogs) and `base` props, and `variant="sheet"` (a full-height sheet from the bottom, with a `backdrop` slot)
    - Effects: `RevealFx`, `LetterFx`, `TypeFx`, `CountFx`, `GlitchFx`, `HoloFx`, `TiltFx`, `FlipFx`, `MatrixFx`, `BlobFx`, `ParticleFx`, `ShineFx`, `CelebrationFx`
    - `HoverCard` (`placement="cursor"` follows the pointer, `"cover"` draws over the trigger), `Dropdown openOn="contextmenu"` (a right-click menu), `Tooltip content` with no children (an info icon), `EmojiPicker trigger`, `Scroller` (track mode with `infinite`/`markers`/`proximity`, or `auto` for a marquee), `Carousel mode="snap"`, `CompareImage`, `OgCard`, `Timeline`, `Grid masonry`, `InfiniteScroll`, `SegmentedControl`, `Kbar` (command palette)
    - Forms: `Input` (`type="password"` has a show/hide toggle), `OTPInput`, `NumberInput`, `TagInput`, `Select`, `DatePicker` (`range` for a date range), `DateInput` (`range`), `ColorInput`, `Slider` (`range` for a `[min, max]` pair), `Switch`, `Checkbox`, `Tag selected`

14. Buttons: `variant` is the appearance, `primary | secondary | tertiary | ghost | link | subtle` (`primary` is the default), and `tone` the palette, `brand | accent | neutral | info | success | warning | danger`: a destructive button is `<Button tone="danger">`; pair with `prefixIcon`/`suffixIcon` (icon names, not elements). `IconButton` for icon-only actions with `tooltip`.

14b. Icon names must come from `iconNames` in catalog.json (spec.json carries the same list). In 2.0 `IconName` is a real union, so an unregistered name is a type error rather than a blank space — do not guess a plausible one, and never reach for `as IconName` to silence the check. If no registered icon fits, omit the icon. The registry is 99 icons; brand marks (github, discord, google) are deliberately not among them, so an app registers its own.

14c. Components with a text prop render it — never pass the same text as both prop and children, it renders twice:

```tsx
// Good
<Tag size="s">{unread}</Tag>  or  <Tag size="s" label="Save 20%" />
// Bad: one of the two is dropped
<Tag label={`${unread} unread`}>{unread}</Tag>
<Tag label="Save 20%">Save 20%</Tag>
```

14d. `Fade` is an **edge overlay strip** (scroll-fade at the boundary of a scroll container), not a content wrapper. Wrapping a message list or section in `Fade` washes the whole content out:

```tsx
// Good: thin absolute strip over the scroll edge
<Column flex={1} overflowY="auto">...</Column>
<Fade position="absolute" top="0" left="0" fillWidth height="40" to="bottom" base="surface" pointerEvents="none" />
// Bad
<Fade to="top" fill><Column overflowY="auto">...</Column></Fade>
```

14e. Multi-part components: a list prop (`items`, `columns`, `options`) for same-shaped data, else plain named parts (`<SortableItem>`, `<StylePanelBrand>`). Never a dotted name (`Sortable.Item`, `StylePanel.Brand`): 3.0 has none, and one fails from a server component.

## Composition rhythm

15. Page skeleton: `Column as="main" fillWidth horizontal="center"` → content `Column maxWidth={...}` → sections. Gaps between siblings, padding inside surfaces; avoid margins for layout when a parent `gap` can do it.

    `maxWidth` conventions: primary page containers `"xl"`–`"m"` (marketing/landing toward `"xl"`/`"l"`, app and docs content `"m"`). `"s"` is only for narrow reading content (about, legal); `"xs"` for special surfaces (drawers, popovers).

16. One-off theme overrides on a subtree, not custom CSS. On `Flex`/`Row`/`Column`/`Grid`, and on every component built on them whose slice lists the typed props (`Background`, `Tag`, `RevealFx`, `BlobFx`, …), use the typed props: `theme="dark"`, `themeBorder="rounded"`, `themeSolid="contrast"`, `themeSurface="translucent"` (they write `data-theme`, `data-border`, `data-solid`, `data-surface`). Attributes without a prop stay raw: `data-brand="emerald"`, and `data-border="rounded"` on `Button` and `IconButton`, which have no typed prop. `theme="dark"` makes a subtree dark; the `dark` boolean only shows an element in a dark theme.

## Scale and hierarchy (marketing/landing pages)

17. Vertical rhythm is generous. Gap between page sections: `"80"`–`"160"` (typical `"104"`). Gap inside a section: `"24"`–`"40"`. Spacing tokens go up to `"160"` — use the top of the scale between sections, not `"48"`.

18. Heading scale: hero = `display-strong-l` (or `xl`), section headings = `display-strong-xs` or `display-strong-s` — never `heading-*` variants for section titles. Hero supporting text = `body-default-l`; section supporting text = `body-default-m`.

19. Type hierarchy must be monotonic: quotes, testimonials, and body content never render larger than the section heading above them. Testimonial quotes = `body-default-m` max, not `BlockQuote` default size.

20. Don't repeat the same centered heading + subtitle block for every section — it reads dated. Vary: left-aligned headers, heading-only sections, or an eyebrow label above the heading. Eyebrow = plain text, not a `Tag` with an icon:

```tsx
// Good eyebrow
<Text textVariant="label-default-s" onBackground="brand-medium">Pricing</Text>
// Bad eyebrow
<Tag tone="neutral" prefixIcon="sparkle">Pricing</Tag>
```

20b. **Proportion is a decision, not a leftover.** Two columns in a row finish at
roughly the same place, or one of them is wrong. A tall card beside a strip of
small controls leaves a column of dead space that reads as an unfinished page —
and the fix is almost never more whitespace tokens.

Give the thin side real content instead. Tiles grow to carry their own height,
with a placeholder, a preview, a swatch, a count — something true about the
thing they stand for. Then keep them quiet: low-contrast surfaces, small labels,
no competing headline. A grid of twenty loud tiles takes the section away from
the card it was meant to support.

```tsx
// Bad: a tall card and 20 chips, most of the row empty
<Row fillWidth gap="32">
  <Column flex={1} maxWidth="26rem"><FeatureCard /></Column>
  <Column flex={1}><Row wrap gap="4">{items.map(i => <Button key={i} size="s">{i}</Button>)}</Row></Column>
</Row>

// Good: both sides carry weight, the card still leads
<Row fillWidth gap="32">
  <Column flex={2}><FeatureCard /></Column>
  <Column flex={3}>
    <Grid columns={5} s={{ columns: 3 }} gap="8" fillWidth>
      {items.map(i => (
        <Column key={i} aspectRatio="1 / 1" padding="12" radius="l"
                background="page" border vertical="between">
          {/* a preview of the thing, not just its name */}
        </Column>
      ))}
    </Grid>
  </Column>
</Row>
```

Check it by squinting at the two columns' bottom edges. If one ends halfway up
the other, change the flex ratio, the tile size, or what the tiles contain —
in that order.

## Decorative layers

21. Every absolute decorative layer uses the full recipe — `top="0" left="0"` are required or the layer gets offset by parent padding:

```tsx
<Background position="absolute" top="0" left="0" fill pointerEvents="none" ... />
```

Siblings holding content get `zIndex={1}`. That layer and its content sibling are the whole stacking group — nothing else in the section needs a `zIndex` (rule 3b). `overflow="hidden"` goes on the parent **only when it has a radius** (cards, panels) — clipping a full-bleed section turns the glow into a hard-edged band.

21b. Ambient section layers (hero glows) live on the **full-width section wrapper**, outside the `maxWidth` content column, with generous room (`paddingY="80"`+). Inside a narrow container the gradient gets clipped at the container edge and reads as a misplaced card:

```tsx
// Good: full-bleed section, narrow content inside
<Column fillWidth horizontal="center" paddingY="80">
  <Background position="absolute" top="0" left="0" fill pointerEvents="none" gradient={{...}} />
  <Column zIndex={1} maxWidth="48rem">...</Column>
</Column>
```

22. `Background` gradient units: `x`/`y` place the centre as a percentage string of the container (`"50%"`/`"50%"` = center) or a number on the token scale. `width`/`height` are the ellipse's radii, as a percentage string of the container (`"100%"`, the default) or a number. A soft corner glow is `width: "100%"`–`"200%"`; `"500%"` overshoots the container. `Mask` is the same: `x`/`y` percentage strings, `radius` a CSS length (`"50vh"`, the default) or a number.

23. Color visibility: `*-background-weak` is nearly the page color — it is invisible as an accent. For tints and glows use alpha tokens (`brand-alpha-medium`, `brand-alpha-strong`) or solid tokens (`brand-solid-strong`) and do not stack a low `opacity` on top of an already-weak color.

## Effect units

24. Time is **milliseconds** everywhere: every `duration`, `delay`, `hold` and interval. Stagger with `delay={index * 100}`, never `index * 0.1` (that was 1.8.x, and 2.0 reads it as a tenth of a millisecond, i.e. no stagger at all). That covers `RevealFx` `duration` and `delay`, `ShineFx` and `CountFx` `duration`, `TypeFx` `charDuration`, `delay` and `hold`, `CelebrationFx` and `WeatherFx` `duration` (`5000`, not `5`), `MatrixFx` `bulge.duration`, `FlipFx` `autoFlipInterval`, `Animation`/`HoverCard` `delay` and `duration`, `HoverCard placement="cover"` `hideDelay`, `Skeleton` `delay`. `speed` is only ever a **multiplier** — `1` is the default, `2` twice as fast, `0.5` half — or `"slow"`/`"medium"`/`"fast"` (0.5/1/2), on `MatrixFx`, `WeatherFx`, `ParticleFx`, `CelebrationFx`, `Effect`, `Scroller` `auto.speed`, `GlitchFx` and `LetterFx`. `translateY` as a number is on the token scale (`16` = `"16"` = 1rem) — use a token like `"16"` or `translateY={16}`.

25. `LogoCloud` extends `Grid` — always set `columns` (and responsive overrides), or logos stack in one column: `columns="4" m={{ columns: 3 }} s={{ columns: 2 }}`.
   A logo that changes with the theme is one `Logo` with a source per theme — `<Logo wordmark={{ light: "/logo-light.svg", dark: "/logo-dark.svg" }} />`, and `icon` takes the same pair — not a `<Logo showIn="dark">` beside a `<Logo showIn="light">`. Keep `showIn` for a logo that should only appear in one theme.

26. Use decoration recipes from `recipes.md` verbatim, then adjust. Application shells — a dashboard with a sidebar, a data-driven nav, a two-pane editor — come from `layouts.md` the same way. Budget: at most one ambient background layer per section, ambient motion in at most the hero and final CTA, one accent color family per page.

## Motion

27. Animations are **eye-leading, not eye-grabbing**: they direct attention to the one thing that should be read next, they don't announce themselves. Small distances (`translateY="8"`–`"16"`, i.e. 0.5–1rem, or 8–16 as numbers), short staggers (`delay={index * 100}` max), and only on elements worth leading the eye to — the hero heading, stat numbers, the highlighted card in a set.

28. Do **not** wrap every section in `RevealFx` — uniform entrance animation on everything reads dated and makes scrolling feel slow. Entry-animation budget per page: the hero, plus at most one or two key moments (stats, a card set). Everything else just renders.

28b. Animate **coherent blocks, all-or-none**. Within a sibling set (cards, list items), either every sibling animates with a stagger or none do — never a single item out of the set (e.g. only the highlighted pricing card). For a hero, reveal it as 1–3 stacked chunks with increasing delay (`0 / 100 / 200`), not individual text fragments. One entrance moment per viewport: if the hero animates, the cards below it don't.

29. Trigger below-the-fold animations with `useInViewport`, latched so they play once. `RevealFx` takes `revealed`; `CountFx` has no trigger prop — drive its `value` instead:

```tsx
const ref = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
const inViewport = useInViewport(ref);
const [seen, setSeen] = useState(false);
useEffect(() => {
  if (inViewport) setSeen(true); // latch: useInViewport flips back to false on scroll-out
}, [inViewport]);

<Column ref={ref} gap="16">
  <RevealFx revealed={seen} translateY="8">...</RevealFx>
  <CountFx value={seen ? 2400 : 0} duration={1500} separator="," textVariant="display-strong-m" />
</Column>
```

Without this, mount-timed animations play while still off-screen and the user scrolls into an already-finished state.

their dependencies are optional peers (or, for `EmojiPicker`, a large dataset)
and a root re-export would drag them into every consumer's module graph, or
because they are packages of their own (the effects and the blocks):

| Import | From | Peer the app installs |
|--------|------|-----------------------|
| charts, gauges, chart chrome | `@once-ui-system/core/data` | none |
| `CodeBlock` | `@once-ui-system/core/code` | `prismjs` |
| `MediaUpload` | `@once-ui-system/core/media` | `compressorjs` |
| `MediaAudioPlayer`, `MediaVideoPlayer`, `Scrubber`, `CompareImage` | `@once-ui-system/core/media` | none |
| `EmojiPicker` | `@once-ui-system/core/emoji` | none |
| `Map`, `MapMarker`, `MapMarkers`, `MapPin`, `MapPopup`, `MapCircle`, `useMap` | `@once-ui-system/core/map` | `maplibre-gl` |
| `mdxComponents`, `createMdxComponents`, the `Mdx*` elements | `@once-ui-system/core/mdx` | `prismjs` (for fenced code) |
| the effects: `RevealFx`, `CountFx`, `TypeFx`, `MatrixFx`, `Effect` and every other `*Fx` | `@once-ui-system/fx` | `@once-ui-system/fx` itself |
| `Banner`, `Book`, `LogoCloud`, `ScrollToTop`, `StylePanel`, `StyleOverlay` | `@once-ui-system/blocks` | `@once-ui-system/blocks` itself |

Naming one of these from the root does not resolve, and there are no deep
imports (`@once-ui-system/core/components/…` is not an entry point). The
effects and the blocks are packages of their own, built on core: add
`@once-ui-system/fx` or `@once-ui-system/blocks` to the app's dependencies
before importing from them (the manifest's `imports` row says `install`).
Each component slice in `ai/components/`, each catalog entry, and each hook or
function in `spec.json`'s `functions` carries the specifier to import it from
when it is not the root; `ai/manifest.json`'s `imports` lists every entry
point with its exports.

```tsx
// MDX through Once UI: headings with anchors, SmartLink, Media, CodeBlock, Table
import { MDXRemote } from "next-mdx-remote/rsc";
import { createMdxComponents, MdxHeading } from "@once-ui-system/core/mdx";

const components = createMdxComponents({
  h2: (props) => <MdxHeading as="h2" marginTop="64" {...props} />, // typed against MDX's props
  Pricing, // an app component, used as <Pricing /> in the content
});
<MDXRemote source={source} components={components} />
```

30b. In a **Next.js** app, `LayoutProvider` comes from
`@once-ui-system/core/next`:

```tsx
import { LayoutProvider } from "@once-ui-system/core/next";
```

The root export resolves and renders, which is what makes it easy to miss: it
installs the plain DOM adapters, so `SmartLink`, `Button`/`Card`/`ToggleButton`
with an `href`, `Media`, `Logo`, `MegaMenu` and `Kbar` render a plain `<a>` and
`<img>` — no client-side navigation, no `next/image`, and no error. The
validator flags it (`LayoutProvider.next`) and `--fix` moves the import. An app
that composes `NextAdapterProvider` itself is already covered.

The same entry has the route handlers `OgCard` and `useOgData` call. Each
returns `{ GET }`, checks every address and redirect is public, and answers at
the paths the client defaults to:

```ts
// app/api/og/fetch/route.ts
import { createOgFetchRoute } from "@once-ui-system/core/next";
export const { GET } = createOgFetchRoute();

// app/api/og/proxy/route.ts
import { createOgProxyRoute } from "@once-ui-system/core/next";
export const { GET } = createOgProxyRoute();
```

Do not hand-write these routes with `handleOGFetch` and a `fetch` of your own.

30c. Type `once-ui.config` with `defineConfig` from
`@once-ui-system/core/config` (the dependency-free entry; the root exports it
too). It rejects a misspelt key or value in `style`, `dataStyle` and `fonts`
and keeps the literal types, so the sections spread into the providers with no
casts:

```tsx
// once-ui.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from "@once-ui-system/core/config";
export const { style, dataStyle } = defineConfig({ style: { brand: "cyan", theme: "system" }, dataStyle: { mode: "categorical" } });

// layout.tsx
<ThemeInit config={style} dataStyle={dataStyle} />
<ThemeProvider {...style}><DataThemeProvider {...dataStyle}>...</DataThemeProvider></ThemeProvider>
```

A denser or roomier app is `style.density` (`"compact"`, `"normal"`, `"spacious"`), not a
`size` on every control: Button, IconButton, ToggleButton, SegmentedControl, Tag, Switch,
Checkbox, RadioButton, RadioGroup and Slider with no `size` take s, m or l from it, and
it picks `scaling` 95/100/105 unless `scaling` is set. A `size` on a control still wins.

30d. The theme a visitor starts on is `defaultTheme` in `style`; `ThemeInit`
paints it and `ThemeProvider` lets the visitor change it. `theme: "light"` or

so leave `theme` out (or `"system"`) for a switchable site. Exact brand colours
go in `brandScale`, `accentScale` or `neutralScale`, one colour per step
(`{ 100: "#…", …, 1200: "#…" }`); a seed fills the steps a scale leaves out.
A ramp per theme is `{ light: { … }, dark: { … } }`. The page and filled-surface
colours are `pageBackground` and `surfaceBackground` (a token or CSS colour, or
`{ light, dark }`). All render on the server through `ThemeInit`. Do not
override the semantic variables (`--page-background`, `--brand-solid-strong`…)
in CSS instead.

# Once UI — application layouts

Recipes for the shells a product sits inside, as opposed to the decoration in
`recipes.md`. Each is the shape a working product converged on, not a sketch.

Use them verbatim, then adjust. The values that look arbitrary usually are not —
the notes say which ones matter and why.

All three compile: they are also `ai/examples/app-shell.tsx`, which `pnpm
typecheck` covers, so a renamed prop breaks the recipe rather than leaving it
quietly wrong.

## 1. App shell with a sidebar

The one agents get wrong most often. A dashboard built without this scrolls the
whole document, so the header and sidebar slide away and the nav has to be
scrolled back to.

```tsx
// The drawer is open for the path it was opened on: a link in it closes it.
const [menuPath, setMenuPath] = useState<string | null>(null);
const menuOpen = menuPath === pathname;

<Column fill horizontal="center" flex={1}>
  <Row height="56" fillWidth vertical="center" paddingX="16" gap="8">  {/* 56px: --header-height */}
    <Row hide s={{ hide: false }}>
      <IconButton icon="moreHorizontal" variant="tertiary" tooltip="Menu"
        aria-expanded={menuOpen} onClick={() => setMenuPath(pathname)} />
    </Row>
    {/* logo, search, account */}
  </Row>
  <Row fill paddingX="8">
    <Column s={{ hide: true }} maxWidth="18rem" fitHeight position="sticky" top="56">
      <SideNav nav={nav} pathname={pathname} />
    </Column>
    <Row fill horizontal="center" topRadius="l" overflow="hidden">
      <Row
        height="below-header"
        overflowY="auto"
        topRadius="l"
        horizontal="center"
        fillWidth
        background="surface">
        <Column maxWidth="xl" gap="m" paddingY="32" fitHeight>
          {children}
        </Column>
      </Row>
    </Row>
  </Row>
  <Drawer open={menuOpen} onClose={() => setMenuPath(null)} side="left" size="s" title="Menu" flush>
    <Column paddingTop="64" paddingBottom="16">
      <SideNav nav={nav} pathname={pathname} />
    </Column>
  </Drawer>
</Column>
```

What each part is doing:

- **The pane scrolls, not the page.** `height="below-header"` plus
  `overflowY="auto"` is what keeps the header and sidebar in place. It is
  `calc(100dvh - var(--header-height))`, written once as a utility class:
  `dvh`, not `vh` — on mobile `vh` ignores the browser chrome and the pane runs
  off-screen. Never restate the header height in a `calc()` of your own.
- **`--header-height`** is 56px (`var(--static-space-56)`) by default, the
  header this recipe uses. A shell with a different header sets it once on
  `:root`; `height`, `minHeight` and `maxHeight` all take `"below-header"`,
  and a mobile menu hanging from the header takes `maxHeight="below-header"`.
- **`position="sticky" top="56"`** on the sidebar, matching the header height
  (`top="calc(var(--header-height))"` follows a non-default one). `fitHeight`
  so it does not stretch and fight the sticky.
- **`topRadius="l"` + `background="surface"`** is what makes the content read as
  a panel sitting on the page rather than the page itself. The radius is on the
  top only, since the bottom is off-screen.
- **`s={{ hide: true }}`** rather than a media query. The mobile nav is a
  separate surface, not this one reflowed: a **`Drawer`** from the left,
  holding the same `SideNav`, opened by a header button that only shows at `s`
  (`hide s={{ hide: false }}`). Drawer brings the focus trap, scroll lock,
  Escape and focus return a hand-made overlay misses; `flush` keeps its
  `title` for screen readers only. Tie it to the path it was opened on, as
  above, and following a link closes it without an effect.
- **`maxWidth="xl"`** inside the pane. A dashboard is wider than a document;
  `"m"` is for reading.

## 2. Data-driven navigation

```tsx
import { Nav, NavGroup, NavItem, selectNavHref } from "@once-ui-system/core";

const current = selectNavHref(pathname, nav.flatMap((i) =>
  i.items ? i.items.map((s) => s.href) : [i.href],
));

<Nav fill paddingX="8" aria-label="Main">
  {nav.map((item) =>
    item.items ? (
      <NavGroup
        key={item.key}
        label={item.label}
        icon={item.icon}
        defaultOpen={item.items.some((s) => s.href === current)}>
        {item.items.map((sub) => (
          <NavItem
            key={sub.href}
            href={sub.href}
            label={sub.label}
            badge={sub.badge}
            selected={sub.href === current}
          />
        ))}
      </NavGroup>
    ) : (
      <NavItem
        key={item.href}
        href={item.href}
        icon={item.icon}
        label={item.label}
        selected={item.href === current}
      />
    ),
  )}
</Nav>
```

- **`Nav` sets the look once.** `density="compact"` for a dashboard's 32px
  rows, `variant="subtle"` or `"minimal"` for a docs or chat sidebar,
  `rail={false}` to drop the line down open groups. Every row inside follows.
- **`selectNavHref` over `===` or `startsWith`.** An equality check leaves a
  nested route (`/settings/billing/invoices/42`) with nothing highlighted; a
  prefix check lights the parent up alongside its child. It returns the longest
  href that matches, which is the right one.
- **Compute `current` once** for the whole tree, not per item — a child needs to
  know about its siblings to know it is the deepest match.
- **`defaultOpen` from the match**, so the group holding the current page is open
  on arrival.
- Child items take **no icon**. The rail inside `NavGroup` carries the hierarchy;
  a second column of icons competes with it.

## 3. Editor shell

Two panes and a timeline — the shape of a video editor, a page builder, a
diff view. `ai/examples/editor.tsx` (task bundle `editor`) is the whole page
around it: toolbar, layer list, canvas and a working timeline.

```tsx
<Column fill>
  <SplitView
    fill
    leftPanel={<Column fill overflowY="auto">{/* layers, blocks, files */}</Column>}
    rightPanel={<Column fill overflowY="auto">{/* canvas, preview */}</Column>}
    defaultSplit={0.28}
    minSplit={0.2}
    maxSplit={0.6}
    collapseBelow="s"
    labels={{ left: "Layers", right: "Canvas" }}
  />
  <Scrubber
    duration={duration}
    value={time}
    onValueChange={setTime}
    tracks={tracks}
    onGestureStart={pause}
  />
</Column>
```

- **`overflowY="auto"` on each panel, not on the SplitView.** The divider needs
  the container to stay put while the panes scroll independently.
- **`collapseBelow` + `labels`.** Below the breakpoint the split becomes tabs, and
  `labels` is what they say. Without it the tabs are unlabelled.
- **`onGestureStart` pauses playback.** Scrubbing while playing fights the
  playhead — the drag sets a time, playback immediately moves it.
- **The timeline is a sibling of the split, not inside it.** It spans both panes,
  and putting it in one makes the divider drag it.

## Anti-patterns

- A dashboard with no scrolling pane — the whole document scrolls and the nav
  leaves with it.
- `100vh` in an app shell. Use `100dvh`; `vh` is wrong on mobile the moment the
  browser chrome shows or hides.
- A sticky sidebar without `fitHeight` — it stretches to the row and the sticky
  never engages.
- A mobile menu built from an absolute `Column` and a `zIndex`. Use `Drawer`.
- `pathname === href` or `startsWith` for nav selection. Use `selectNavHref`.
- Icons on both a NavGroup and its children — two columns of icons, no hierarchy.
- `overflow` on the SplitView instead of on its panels — the divider stops
  tracking the pointer.

"use client";

/**
 * Gold example: settings
 * Target: a vertical tab list beside the panel (above it on a phone), a
 * profile form, settings rows with one control each, a group whose
 * sub-settings sit inside it, and a danger zone.
 *
 * The section nav is `Tabs` with `orientation="vertical"`: one `TabPanel` per
 * section, so only the chosen section renders, the list gets the tab roles
 * and arrow keys, and a phone gets the list above the panel from one
 * breakpoint prop. Sections that are routes of their own use `NavItem href`
 * instead. `keepMounted` keeps the profile form's unsaved input when the
 * user looks at another tab.
 *
 * `Setting` is the row — label and description on the left, one control on
 * the right — and stacks into a panel on its own, so a list of them needs no
 * surface around it. With `control` and `open` it is a group that keeps its sub-settings inside its box,
 * which is what keeps the relationship readable in a long panel.
 */
import {
  Avatar,
  Button,
  Column,
  Form,
  Heading,
  Input,
  NumberInput,
  Row,
  Select,
  Setting,
  Switch,
  Tab,
  TabList,
  TabPanel,
  Tabs,
  Text,
  useToast,
} from "@once-ui-system/core";
import { useState } from "react";

export function SettingsExample() {
  // addToast is stable: call it from handlers and effects directly.
  const { addToast } = useToast();
  const [timezone, setTimezone] = useState("utc");
  const [updates, setUpdates] = useState(true);
  const [digest, setDigest] = useState(true);
  const [digestHour, setDigestHour] = useState(9);

  return (
    <Column as="main" fillWidth horizontal="center" paddingY="48" paddingX="24">
      <Column maxWidth="l" gap="40">
        <Column gap="12">
          <Text textVariant="label-default-s" onBackground="brand-medium">
            Settings
          </Text>
          <Heading as="h1" textVariant="display-strong-s">
            Manage your workspace
          </Heading>
        </Column>

        <Tabs defaultValue="profile" orientation="vertical" gap="32" s={{ direction: "column" }}>
          <TabList aria-label="Settings sections" minWidth="14rem" s={{ direction: "row" }}>
            <Tab value="profile" size="l" prefixIcon="person">
              Profile
            </Tab>
            <Tab value="notifications" size="l" prefixIcon="bell">
              Notifications
            </Tab>
            <Tab value="workspace" size="l" prefixIcon="settings">
              Workspace
            </Tab>
          </TabList>

          <TabPanel value="profile" keepMounted>
            <Column background="surface" border radius="l" padding="24" gap="24">
              <Heading as="h2" textVariant="heading-strong-m">
                Profile
              </Heading>
              <Row gap="16" vertical="center">
                <Avatar size="l" value="AP" />
                <Column gap="8">
                  <Button size="s" variant="secondary">
                    Upload photo
                  </Button>
                  <Text textVariant="label-default-s" onBackground="neutral-weak">
                    JPG or PNG, max 2 MB
                  </Text>
                </Column>
              </Row>
              <Form
                as="form"
                columns={{ xl: 2, s: 1 }}
                onSubmit={(event) => event.preventDefault()}
              >
                <Input id="name" label="Display name" />
                <Input id="email" label="Email" type="email" />
                <Select
                  id="timezone"
                  label="Timezone"
                  value={timezone}
                  onValueChange={(value) => setTimezone(value as string)}
                  options={[
                    { value: "utc", label: "UTC" },
                    { value: "cet", label: "Central European Time" },
                    { value: "est", label: "Eastern Time" },
                  ]}
                />
              </Form>
              <Row gap="12">
                <Button onClick={() => addToast({ tone: "success", message: "Profile saved" })}>
                  Save changes
                </Button>
                <Button variant="secondary">Cancel</Button>
              </Row>
            </Column>
          </TabPanel>

          <TabPanel value="notifications" gap="8">
            <Heading as="h2" textVariant="heading-strong-m" marginBottom="8">
              Notifications
            </Heading>
            <Setting label="Product updates" description="Release notes and changelog">
              <Switch
                checked={updates}
                onCheckedChange={() => setUpdates(!updates)}
                aria-label="Product updates"
              />
            </Setting>
            <Setting
              label="Weekly digest"
              info="A summary of the week's activity, sent once."
              control={
                <Switch
                  checked={digest}
                  onCheckedChange={() => setDigest(!digest)}
                  aria-label="Weekly digest"
                />
              }
              open={digest}
            >
              <Setting label="Send at" description="Hour of the day, in your timezone">
                <NumberInput
                  id="digest-hour"
                  min={0}
                  max={23}
                  value={digestHour}
                  onValueChange={setDigestHour}
                />
              </Setting>
            </Setting>
          </TabPanel>

          <TabPanel value="workspace">
            <Column
              background="surface"
              border="danger-alpha-medium"
              radius="l"
              padding="24"
              gap="16"
            >
              <Heading as="h2" textVariant="heading-strong-m" onBackground="danger-medium">
                Danger zone
              </Heading>
              <Text textVariant="body-default-s" onBackground="neutral-weak">
                Permanently delete your workspace and all associated data.
              </Text>
              <Row>
                <Button tone="danger" size="s">
                  Delete workspace
                </Button>
              </Row>
            </Column>
          </TabPanel>
        </Tabs>
      </Column>
    </Column>
  );
}

Write the page from it; reading the rules, catalog, gotchas, manifest or examples again only adds cost. Open `components/.json` only for a component not listed here, and then every one you need in a single step. ## Rules ### Layout | Write | Never write | |-------|-------------| | `` | `` | | `` | ``, or `` with no direction | | `fill` | `fillWidth fillHeight` | | `fit` | `fitWidth fitHeight` | | `center` | `horizontal="center" vertical="center"` | | `maxWidth="l"` | `fillWidth maxWidth="l"` | | `fillWidth` | `fillWidth minWidth={0}` | | `width={32} height={32}` (a number is the token: `32` = `"32"` = 2rem), `maxWidth="40rem"` | `maxWidth={40}` for 40rem (that was 2.x: `40` is now `"40"`, 2.5rem) | | `border` | `border="neutral-alpha-weak"` | | `` | a `` and a `` | - Units: a number is on the **token scale** on every size, spacing and offset prop: `16` = `"16"` = 1rem, scaled by `data-scaling` (`width={320}`, `padding={24}`, `top={8}`), in breakpoint objects too; a digit string is the spacing token (`"16"`); any CSS length string passes through (`"320px"` never scales, `"50%"`, `"100dvh"`). `Mask`/`Background` percentages are strings (`x="50%"`) - Control size for a whole app: `density: "compact" | "normal" | "spacious"` in the config `style` (`data-density`), not `size="s"` on every Button; it also picks scaling 95/100/105 unless `scaling` is set. Give `size` only where one control differs - `Flex` only when direction changes at breakpoints: `` - Subtree theme: `theme`, `themeBorder`, `themeSolid`, `themeSurface` on Flex/Row/Column/Grid and components built on them (`Background`, `Tag`, effects) — not raw `data-theme`/`data-border`/`data-solid`. `Button`/`IconButton` have no typed prop: keep `data-border="rounded"` - App theme in `once-ui.config` `style`: `defaultTheme: "light"` = starts light, visitor can switch (`theme: "light"` forces it and `setTheme` does nothing). Exact brand colours: `brandScale`/`neutralScale` `{ 100: "#…", …, 1200: "#…" }` (with or without a seed; per theme `{ light: {…}, dark: {…} }`), page/card colour: `pageBackground`/`surfaceBackground` (token or colour, or `{ light, dark }`), not overrides of semantic CSS variables - Page skeleton: `Column as="main" fillWidth horizontal="center"` → content `Column maxWidth="l"` → sections - Section gaps: `"104"` between sections, `"24"`–`"40"` inside. Never `"48"` between major sections. - Responsive: breakpoint props `xl l m s xs` — never media queries for layout ### Surfaces Static panel recipe (pricing tiers, stats, settings sections): ```tsx ``` - Bare `border` (and `borderTop`, `borderBottom`, …) = the default border. Name a colour only to deviate: `border="brand-alpha-medium"`. - `Card` = interactive only (`href` or `onClick`). Static panels = Column + surface recipe. - Colors: `{tone}-{weight}` or `{tone}-alpha-{weight}`. Never hex/rgb — inline SVG `fill`/`stroke` included: `currentColor` or `var(--brand-solid-strong)`. - `background` also: `surface | overlay | page | transparent` ### Typography - Hero: `display-strong-l` or `display-strong-xl` - Section titles: `display-strong-xs` or `display-strong-s` — not `heading-*` - Eyebrow: `` - Text on layout: `textVariant` + `onBackground` on Row/Column instead of nesting Text ### Decoration Absolute layers always: `position="absolute" top="0" left="0" fill pointerEvents="none"`, content `zIndex={1}`. - `zIndex` only inside that layer group (or on a sticky header over its pane). Never on a lone element, never a page-wide ladder. - Gradient `width`: quarter-percent (400 = 100%). Glows: 100–200. - Glow colors: `brand-alpha-medium`, not `brand-background-weak` - Ambient layers on full-bleed section wrapper, outside `maxWidth` column - Budget: one ambient layer per section; motion in hero + one CTA max ### Motion - Every `duration`, `delay` and interval is **milliseconds**: `delay={index * 100}` — `* 0.1` was 1.8.x; `CelebrationFx`/`WeatherFx` `duration={5000}`, not `{5}`. `RevealFx`/`ShineFx`/`CountFx` take `duration`, `TypeFx` `charDuration` (`speed` there was 2.x) - `speed` is only a multiplier, `1` the default, or `"slow"`/`"medium"`/`"fast"` (0.5/1/2): `MatrixFx`, `WeatherFx`, `ParticleFx`, `CelebrationFx`, `Effect`, `Scroller` `auto.speed`, `GlitchFx`, `LetterFx` - `RevealFx translateY`: a number is the token scale (`16` = 1rem); prefer `"8"`–`"16"` tokens - Viewport-reveal with `useInViewport` + latch into `RevealFx revealed`; `CountFx` driven by `value`, no trigger prop - Animate all siblings in a set or none — never one lone animated card ### Components | Need | Use | |------|-----| | Image | `Media` | | Link | `SmartLink` / `Button href` | | Status dot | `StatusIndicator` | | Loading | `Spinner` / `Skeleton` | | Scroll fade | `Fade` as edge strip, not wrapper | | Icons | `IconName` (the IconName type below) only | | Logos grid | `LogoCloud` with `columns` set | | Tabs | `Tabs` > `TabList` > `Tab`, `TabPanel` (`orientation="vertical"` for a settings nav) | | Mobile nav, side sheet | `Drawer`, not a hand-made overlay | | Page trail | `Breadcrumbs items={[...]}` | | Keyboard shortcut | `useHotkeys("mod+k", fn)` + `Kbd keys="mod+k" label="Search"` | | Screen-reader text, skip link | `VisuallyHidden` (skip link: ``) | | Native attributes | Every component also takes its element's own: `aria-*`, `id`, `role`, `onClick`; `type` on `Button`; `value`, `onChange`, `type` on `Input` | | MDX content | `mdxComponents` / `createMdxComponents` from `/mdx` | | Multi-part component | List prop (`items`, `columns`, `options`) for same-shaped data, else plain named parts (`SortableItem`, `StylePanelBrand`); never `Sortable.Item` | ### Imports Most things come from the package root. These do not — each component below says where it comes from when it is not the root: | Import | From | |--------|------| | charts, gauges, chart chrome | `@once-ui-system/core/data` | | `CodeBlock` | `@once-ui-system/core/code` (needs `prismjs`) | | `MediaUpload` | `@once-ui-system/core/media` (needs `compressorjs`) | | `Map`, `MapMarker(s)`, `MapPin`, `MapPopup`, `MapCircle` | `@once-ui-system/core/map` (needs `maplibre-gl`) | | `mdxComponents`, `createMdxComponents`, `Mdx*` elements | `@once-ui-system/core/mdx` (needs `prismjs`) | | `MediaAudioPlayer`, `MediaVideoPlayer`, `Scrubber`, `CompareImage` | `@once-ui-system/core/media` | | `EmojiPicker` | `@once-ui-system/core/emoji` | | `LayoutProvider` in a **Next.js** app; `createOgFetchRoute`, `createOgProxyRoute` | `@once-ui-system/core/next` | | `defineConfig`, `OnceUIConfig` in `once-ui.config` | `@once-ui-system/core/config` (also on the root) | | the effects: `RevealFx`, `CountFx`, `TypeFx`, `MatrixFx`, `Effect`, every `*Fx` | `@once-ui-system/fx` (a package: install it) | | `Banner`, `Book`, `LogoCloud`, `ScrollToTop`, `StylePanel`, `StyleOverlay` | `@once-ui-system/blocks` (a package: install it) | Naming one of these from the root does not resolve — except `defineConfig`, which is on both, and `LayoutProvider`, which resolves and then silently renders links and images as plain `` and `` in a Next.js app. `IconName` is a real union, so an unregistered icon name is a type error, not a blank space — take names (the IconName type below). Brand marks are not in the set: an app registers them by augmenting `IconLibraryOverrides`. ### Types — the common type errors Every type a prop names is defined in the slice's (or bundle's) `types`. - Responsive `xl`/`l`/`m`/`s`/`xs` props exist only on `Flex`, `Row`, `Column` and `Grid`. To change a `Button`, `Text` or anything else at a breakpoint, wrap it in one of those; `Text` and `Heading` take only `s={{ hide: true }}`. Leaves (`Button`, the fields and controls, `Text`, `Heading`, `Icon`, `Avatar`, `Kbd`…) take only margins, `flex`, `fillWidth`, `position` and offsets, `className` and `style`: padding, background, border, radius, sizes and anything else at a breakpoint go on a wrapper too. - `vertical`/`horizontal` take `start | center | end | between | around | even | stretch` — no `baseline`; for baseline-aligned text write `style={{ alignItems: "baseline" }}`. - Spacing (`gap`, `padding`, …) takes the SpacingToken values below: `"4"`, `"8"`, `"12"`, `"16"`, `"20"`, `"24"`, `"32"`, `"40"`… — there is no `"6"` or `"10"`. - `as` on `Flex`/`Row`/`Column`/`Grid` types the element's attributes and ref: ``, ``. `as="ul"`/`"ol"` drops bullets and indent, `as="button"` the button chrome; other components take no `as`. - `Row`, `Column` and `Grid` have no `span`: a child spanning grid columns uses `style={{ gridColumn: "span 2" }}`. - `variant` is appearance (Button: `primary | secondary | tertiary | ghost | link`), `tone` the palette (`brand | accent | neutral | info | success | warning | danger`) on Button, IconButton, Tag, Feedback, Toast and `addToast`: ` setFilter(value as Filter)} buttons={[ { value: "all", label: "All" }, { value: "active", label: "Active" }, { value: "invited", label: "Invited" }, { value: "suspended", label: "Suspended" }, ]} /> No members match this filter. } columns={[ { header: "Name", key: "name", sortable: true }, { header: "Role", key: "role", sortable: true }, { header: "Status", key: "status", sortable: true }, { header: "Last active", key: "lastActive", sortable: true, align: "right" }, ]} rows={visible.map((member) => [ {member.name} {member.email} , member.role, {statusTag[member.status].label} , member.lastActive, ])} perPageOptions={[5, 10, 20, 50]} showFirstLast actions={[ { icon: "edit", tooltip: "Edit member", onClick: (_row, index) => onEdit?.(visible[index]), }, { icon: "trash", tooltip: "Remove member", variant: "primary", tone: "danger", onClick: (_row, index) => onRemove?.(visible[index]), }, ]} /> );
